summary: The bill amends the Federal Power Act to direct FERC to presume that using the highest-capacity, most efficient commercially available transmission conductors on new or upgraded lines is prudent with recoverable costs, while presuming the opposite for lesser conductors, and to issue implementing rules within 180 days.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Federal Power Act to set standards for transmission conductors and create FERC presumptions on cost recovery for utilities. It regulates private utility rate filings but does not authorize, expand, or reduce any federal government spending or appropriations.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill concerns electric transmission infrastructure and has no connection to healthcare policy or systems.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, or pathways.
No provisions relate to reproductive health or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending or policy.

The bill promotes high-efficiency transmission conductors but does not reference environmental protections, emissions, climate policy, or regulations. Any efficiency gains are incidental to grid infrastructure standards rather than genuine engagement with environmental topics.
